Definition: from G1909 and G3618; to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up:--build thereon (thereupon, on, upon).
BiblicalUsage: Epoikodoméō means to build upon — to rear up on a foundation already laid. Paul lays the foundation and another builds on it; the church is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets; and believers are built up together into a holy temple. It is the word for the church's construction.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe epoikodoméō is the word for the church: one foundation, many builders, and Christ the cornerstone. I hold that I am both a builder and a stone, and I should take care how I build.
